title: The testimony in the sitting
hookLine: the finger raised, the greeting on the Prophet ﷺ and the righteous
carry: peace on us and the good

lines: A HAND HELD BETWEEN TWO PALMS.
cards: A companion named Ibn Mas'ud remembered how he learned today's words. Not from a page, and not in passing.
The Prophet ﷺ held Ibn Mas'ud's hand between his own two palms, the way a grandparent holds a child's hand to shape a letter, and taught him the words the way he'd teach a chapter of the Qur'an.
At the end of every second unit of prayer, and at the very end, the person sits and says them, and near the end, lifts one finger.

teach.b: It's called tashahhud, from the root for witnessing, because it ends with the testimony: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger.
As the person says it, the index finger of the right hand is raised, pointing to the one God. The schools differ on exactly when to raise it and whether to move it.
But it begins with a greeting, and there's a story in Bukhari about how that came to be.
Ibn Mas'ud said that early on, the companions would say in the sitting: peace be on Allah, peace on Jibril, peace on Mika'il, peace on so-and-so.
The Prophet turned to them and said: don't say peace be on Allah, for Allah is Himself the Peace. Say instead: at-tahiyyatu lillah, all greetings are for Allah, and the prayers and the good things.
Peace be on you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be on us and on the righteous servants of Allah.
Then he added one more thing: when you say that, it reaches every righteous servant in the heavens and on the earth. Not just friends. Not just one community.

teach.h: PEACE ON US AND THE GOOD.
teach.b: Someone sitting on the floor of one small room sends peace to all of them.

how: After every second unit and at the end of each prayer, Muslims sit and recite the tashahhud, beginning at-tahiyyatu lillah and ending with the testimony of faith, raising the right index finger as they bear witness.

o: a hymn sung together after the sermon
a private prayer said once the prayer ends
the seated words that end in the testimony

games.q: what's inside the tashahhud — tap the pairs.

s: the companions once said peace be on Allah in the sitting
the Prophet ﷺ told them Allah is Himself the Peace, and taught the tashahhud instead (Bukhari).
the greeting in the tashahhud is only for people in the room
the hadith says it reaches every righteous servant in the heavens and on the earth.
all schools raise the finger at exactly the same moment
they differ on when to raise it and whether to move it.

games.q: you're sitting in prayer with the companions, saying: peace be on Allah, peace on Jibril, peace on Mika'il. the Prophet ﷺ turns to you. what does he say?
o: keep going, and add more names
don't say peace on Allah, for Allah is the Peace
games.why: he taught them at-tahiyyatu lillah instead, and said the greeting on the righteous reaches every one of them in heaven and earth (Bukhari).

practice: Sit with your hands resting on your thighs, and say the first line slowly, three times: at-tahiyyatu lillah, all greetings are for Allah. If you pray, you can go on: was-salawatu wat-tayyibat, and the prayers and the good things.
If you don't, hold the image of peace going out from where you sit to every good person, everywhere, and keep one of them you know by name in mind.

wordCard.voice: Tashahhud. The testimony in the sitting: greetings to Allah, peace on the Prophet, on us and on the righteous, then the witness, finger raised. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: all greetings are for Allah, the opening of the tashahhud.

carryVoice: Your line: peace on us and the good. The greeting travels much further than the room. That's day one hundred seven.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 831 (don't say peace on Allah; the tashahhud; it reaches every righteous servant)
Sahih al-Bukhari 6265 (taught with his hand between the Prophet's palms, as a surah is taught)
Qur'an 59:23 (al-Salam among the names of Allah)
